basis: No filed findings; items 0-3 are outside the window and 4-10 found nothing; statutory accounts of a quarterly-report filer were non-events before (item 5). Casebook: hunts with no findings carry no edge.

basis: Item 0: the P&L was pre-announced, so this is a confirmation event, and past final-results prints moved slightly down. Items 1-2: flat adjusted EPS and a capped buyback are mild negatives.
against: A dividend increase or upbeat current trading could lift a thin AIM name that has drifted near its lows.

basis: Item 0: the interim dividend formula points to an increase after a -26% de-rate, and items 1 and 3 say the numbers were pre-released and the shorts are quant. Item 2's H2-weighted guide offsets most of it.
against: The board cut guidance only 47 days after reassuring, and a print defending the most H2-weighted year it has ever guided can disappoint again.

basis: Item 1: an activist TR-1 crossing 9%, published after the entry close, a dated hard fact. Item 0: the Australian closure is reported only in Australian trade press and the prior 'removing Australia' framing was paid up (+3.9%). Item 2: a buyback relaunch is a possible lever.
against: Closure costs and a cut to the FY27 revenue consensus could read negatively; the last Australia-heavy interim was -12%.

basis: Item 0: about EUR 12m of board-linked buying inside the 30 days before results whose quarter had already closed, plus no ad-hoc since June. A 5.4% short that is slowly covering, and back-to-normal events have been bought (+4% to +6%).
against: A cash-flow or covenant disappointment on a leverage-heavy balance sheet can sink an in-line print, and the history is cadence-estimated.

basis: Item 0: the dividend has come in below FactSet two years running and the step pattern points below 3.53. Item 2: the sales consensus likely assumes property gains that have not been announced. Item 1's group bookings figure is a small offset.
against: Bookings at +3-6% would be the best year-end reading in three years and the stock has already fallen 7.7% from its August high.

basis: Item 0: zero FPDS federal actions in the fiscal-year-end obligation month plus a DOE deobligation. Item 2: board departures. Six of the last eight prints fell and put skew is +19; this matches the casebook pattern of a primary-record datapoint covering the quarter.
against: With 32% of float short and the defence hiring build in item 1, any decent guide could squeeze it hard, and FPDS can show a false zero for OTAs and marketplace sales.

basis: Two independent hunters converge on hard industry series covering the exact quarter: zero Silver Eagle sales in May (item 0), premiums collapsing (items 1 and 11), WGC bar-and-coin demand -36% (item 11) and JM Bullion traffic (item 2), against a single $0.96 estimate and extreme operating leverage (item 3). This is the SWBI/SPWH pattern (quarter-aligned industry data), with the sign reversed.
against: Item 12: this holder base barely reacts to EPS (+0.95% on a 4.5x beat), and the full-year headline will read as a record (item 13), so the print could be looked through.

basis: Items 0 and 2: unguided IEEPA refund upside and positive August pet-category peer reads. Item 3: 21% of float short with a history of big up moves (5 of the last 7 prints up).
against: Casebook: tariff-refund long theses failed repeatedly (LOVE, VNCE) because the market strips refunds out, and the diesel point in item 1 threatens the H2 guide.

basis: Item 0: stale consensus means a guaranteed ~26% revenue-miss headline. Item 1: an open impairment review on $88m of assets against a $68m market cap, under a new CFO. Item 2: the last two real prints fell 44% and 24%. Matches the casebook pattern of distressed microcaps with documented negative filings (BIOX, HYFT, COE, IPHA).
against: Item 3: every bad fact is already disclosed and the stock just rallied 22% off its lows, so a de-risked print could squeeze shorts.

basis: Item 0 (buyback throttled by about 85%) and item 1 (peers raised guidance, a de-rate that is sector beta, Q1 event revenue) offset each other.
against: Either leg could dominate: a margin miss confirms JPM's thesis, a strong peer-like quarter squeezes a stock 14% lower over 20 days.

basis: Item 0: the Q4 ARR guide is set by an interim CFO with the segment head leaving. Item 1: free ChatGPT access lands in the guide window. Six of the last seven prints were down, and the call-bid skew is not positioned for a soft guide.
against: The stock is already down 10% in five days on the succession news, and item 2 (Figma deceleration) plus a buyback could make a fine guide a relief rally.

basis: Item 0: the competitor's same-months disclosure (+11% units on share gains in a flat industry) implies Copart's US insurance units fell 5-7%. against: Total-loss frequency is at a record and ASP is up, so revenue can hold even on fewer units; the implied move is only 4.8%.

basis: Items 0-1: a liquidity squeeze mid-quarter and lost Elcom revenue against a consensus calling for +29%. Item 3: a lock-up expires shortly after.
against: Item 2: a likely record-backlog headline, the very thing behind this stock's two biggest positive reactions (+30%, +29%).

basis: Item 2: same-window peer reads (Walmart, Costco, Ahold) show traffic leaving conventional grocers. Item 1: the new CEO's team is seated, which sets up a guidance reset. Item 0: a buyback running at 10% of plan. The casebook's new-management reset pattern (AEO, SKIL) was right.
against: Item 3: hotter food inflation could produce a comp beat, and the call-bid skew leans up.

basis: Item 0: the unexecuted $20bn ATM with newly added agents caps the upside after a 37% rally. Item 1: a dated power delay at a flagship campus.
against: This stock trades on RPO and AI deal headlines that neither item touches, and the skew is call-bid.

basis: Item 0: an unguided tariff refund that peer WSM collected in the same quarter, on a stock down 23% over 20 days with +18.6 put skew (positioned for bad news).
against: Casebook: tariff-refund longs (LOVE, VNCE) repeatedly fell hard; item 1 (the Estates ramp) and item 2 (the CEO's personal leverage) point down.
